classification.habitat: Moist rocky slopes, shaded mountain habitats and stream-side sites
classification.distribution: Himalayan and adjoining mountainous regions of the Indian subcontinent

identification.description: Small perennial herb with thick rhizomes, basal leathery leaves and clustered flowers; rhizome is the principal crude drug.
identification.whole_plant: Low-growing perennial herb arising from a stout creeping rhizome.
identification.root: Fibrous roots arise from the rhizome.
identification.stem: Short flowering scape arising from the basal rosette.
identification.leaf: Large, rounded to broadly ovate, leathery basal leaves with long petioles and prominent venation.
identification.flower: White to pink flowers borne in terminal clusters on a leafless scape.
identification.seed: Numerous very small seeds within the capsule.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a herbaceous plant.

therapeutics.precautions: Urinary stone disease may require medical assessment; this educational record does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Bergenin is a characteristic reported constituent of Bergenia species; composition varies with plant part and preparation.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Bergenia ligulata has been investigated in urinary and antioxidant-related experimental research. Evidence should be interpreted according to preparation and study quality.
modern_information.safety_notes: Persistent urinary pain, fever, obstruction or blood in urine requires appropriate medical evaluation.

viva_questions: What is the useful part of Pashanabheda?
Which family is traditionally listed for Bergenia ligulata?
mnemonics: Pashanabheda = stone-breaker name; remember stout rhizome and basal leaves.
student.quick_revision: Pashanabheda (Bergenia ligulata): perennial rhizomatous herb; rhizome is used; large leathery basal leaves and pink-white flowers aid identification.

teaching_points: Demonstrate rhizome and basal leaf morphology.
Discuss the limits of equating a traditional name with modern clinical action.
practical_points: Inspect rhizome surface and internal texture.
Observe leaf venation and flowering scape.

doctor.quick_reference: Pashanabheda is traditionally associated with Mutravaha and Ashmari indications; persistent urinary symptoms require proper assessment.
key_precautions: Do not delay evaluation of obstruction or infection symptoms
Use verified therapeutic references for dosing
